issues.description: The problem statement (UML) declares the Pneumatic interface with methods raisePressure(int) and openValve(). In the solution, Pneumatic.java declares raisePressure(int) and releaseValve(), while the implementing classes (LaunchedDropdownTower, LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement an openValve() method. This name/signature mismatch between the interface and its implementations contradicts the UML and will cause compilation errors and confusion for students about the correct method name.
issues.suggested_fix: Make the interface method name match the UML and the implementing classes. For example, rename releaseValve() in Pneumatic.java to openValve(), or alternatively rename the openValve() methods in the implementing classes to releaseValve(). Prefer changing the interface to openValve() to match the problem statement UML and tests.

issues.description: The UML/problem statement defines the Pneumatic interface with an abstract method openValve(), but the solution implementation declares that method as releaseValve() in Pneumatic. Meanwhile the solution's concrete classes (LaunchedDropdownTower and LaunchedRollerCoaster) implement a method named openValve(). This produces a naming mismatch: the interface in the solution uses a different identifier (releaseValve) than the UML and the classes (openValve). Students following the problem/UML will expect openValve() on the Pneumatic interface; the solution's different name breaks the clear one-to-one mapping and can cause confusion and compilation inconsistency.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the Pneumatic interface name with the UML/problem: replace releaseValve() with openValve() in the Pneumatic interface (in solution and template). Ensure all implementing classes declare/override openValve() to match the interface. Alternatively, if the intended name is releaseValve(), update the problem statement/UML to use releaseValve() so all artifacts use the same identifier.
